diff_summary.old_string:
"""Implementations of the Bench CLI commands (verify, ledger, stats,
constitution, viewer).

Each command returns an int exit code (0 on success, 1 on failure) and
prints a human-readable summary to stdout. Error diagnostics go to stderr
so the two streams can be separated in scripts.

These commands are read-only reports over the ledger and constitution —
nothing here mutates state, so there is no risk of collision with the
governance pipeline running in parallel.
"""
diff_summary.new_string:
"""Implementations of the Bench CLI commands (verify, ledger, stats,
constitution, viewer, retire, audit-retirement).

Each command returns an int exit code (0 on success, 1 on failure) and
prints a human-readable summary to stdout. Error diagnostics go to stderr
so the two streams can be separated in scripts.

All but one of these are read-only reports over the ledger and constitution,
so there is no risk of collision with the governance pipeline running in
parallel. The exception is ``cmd_retire``, which archives the active chain and
opens a successor under C-008's single bounded exception to ledger
immutability. It holds no logic of its own: every decision, guard, and write
lives in ``ledger/retire.py``, and this module only parses arguments, supplies
the real ``sys.stdin.isatty`` and ``input``, and renders the result.
"""

findings.evidence: "cmd_retire, which archives the active chain and opens a successor under C-008's single bounded exception to ledger immutability... every decision, guard, and write lives in ``ledger/retire.py``"
findings.reasoning: The docstring asserts that a specific command performs the sole permitted exception to ledger immutability (chain retirement) and that all guards/decisions live in ledger/retire.py. This diff contains only the doc comment, not ledger/retire.py or the actual cmd_retire implementation. Whether the described behavior actually satisfies all of C-008's enumerated requirements (human-triggered decision recorded in anchor, pre-move verification of archive, anchor entry with tip hash/genesis/counts/timestamps/path/reason, indefinite retention) cannot be verified from this file alone. The claim should be checked against the actual retire.py diff before being taken as established fact.

findings.evidence: "Implementations of the Bench CLI commands (verify, ledger, stats, constitution, viewer, retire, audit-retirement)"
findings.reasoning: cli/ is not listed among pipeline/, ledger/, or hooks/ in CLAUDE.md's C-007 trigger list, yet this docstring now documents a command (cmd_retire) whose purpose is to mutate ledger state (via delegation). Since this file is the entry point that invokes ledger retirement, changes to it that affect retire behavior arguably fall within the spirit of C-007 self-governance scrutiny even though the constitution's file list doesn't name cli/ explicitly. Not a violation of this docstring-only change, but worth flagging so the actual cmd_retire logic (wherever it lands) receives the same C-007 scrutiny as pipeline/ledger/hooks files.

findings.evidence: Entire diff is a docstring update referencing new commands 'retire' and 'audit-retirement' and a new file 'ledger/retire.py' that are not shown in this change.
findings.reasoning: This change is coherent on its own (documentation update), but it references functionality (retire command, ledger/retire.py) implemented elsewhere and not included in this diff. This is not itself a scope violation, but confirms the full feature is split across multiple tool calls; the retire.py implementation should be reviewed on its own merits against C-008 and C-007 rather than assumed compliant based on this comment alone.

rebuttals.argument: The Challenger is right that this diff alone cannot prove retire.py satisfies C-008(a)-(d), and correctly stops short of calling it a violation, filing it as a CONCERN rather than a finding against this change. But note what this diff actually does: it is a docstring edit to commands.py, and the constraint text of C-008 prohibits modifying, deleting, or overwriting ledger entries. A comment describing an architecture cannot itself violate that rule; only the code that performs the archive-and-anchor sequence can. What the docstring gets right, and what matters for evaluating *this* diff, is the division of responsibility it documents: 'every decision, guard, and write lives in ledger/retire.py,' meaning commands.py is asserted to hold no retirement logic of its own, only argument parsing and rendering. That is the correct shape for a change touching a command surface adjacent to a veto-severity constraint: keep the CLI thin, keep the guarded logic centralized and auditable in one file. The verifiability gap the Challenger flags is real, but it is a gap to be closed by reviewing ledger/retire.py on its own diff, exactly as the Challenger recommends, not a defect in this one.
rebuttals.evidence: new_string: 'It holds no logic of its own: every decision, guard, and write lives in ``ledger/retire.py``, and this module only parses arguments, supplies the real ``sys.stdin.isatty`` and ``input``, and renders the result.' The change_type is 'modify' to a docstring only; no ledger read/write code is present in the diff.

rebuttals.argument: This is a fair and useful process observation, and the Challenger already frames it correctly: 'Not a violation of this docstring-only change.' I won't argue it isn't worth tracking, cli/commands.py is the entry point that triggers ledger mutation via delegation, so when the actual cmd_retire implementation (or any future direct ledger-touching code) lands in this file, it deserves the same C-007-level scrutiny as pipeline/ledger/hooks changes even though the constitution's constraint text and CLAUDE.md's file list don't name cli/ explicitly. I'd only add: the constitution's own C-007 text lists 'challenger, defender, oracle, ledger, constitution' as the scope, and cli/ is absent from that list too, not just from CLAUDE.md's summary, so there's no textual violation to concede here, just a sound recommendation for future diffs in this file.
rebuttals.evidence: Constraint C-007 rule text: 'Changes to the governance pipeline itself (challenger, defender, oracle, ledger, constitution) must not weaken enforcement...' cli/ is not enumerated.

rebuttals.argument: The Challenger explicitly concludes this is 'not itself a scope violation,' and I agree. The docstring update is a single coherent edit describing the module's current role, consistent with CLAUDE.md rule 14 ('one change per tool call'), which is exactly why a multi-file feature like retire/audit-retirement naturally lands as sequential, individually-reviewable diffs rather than one giant batch. Documenting a dependency on a file not included in this particular diff is normal incremental development, not scope creep, especially since C-002 explicitly protects against being vetoed for lacking an in-band task description while still requiring internal coherence, which this diff has.
rebuttals.evidence: Diff is confined to one docstring in commands.py; C-002 constraint text: 'The absence of a stated task description is not itself a violation... an author has no in-band way to supply one.'

raw_response.summary: This diff is a documentation-only change that accurately and modestly describes a thin CLI layer delegating all ledger-retirement logic to ledger/retire.py, and all three Challenger findings are self-labeled OBSERVATION/CONCERN rather than violations, correctly leaving the substantive C-008/C-007 compliance question to be judged against retire.py's own diff.
